stories.headline: Modi's two-day Norway visit: bilateral agreements, India-Nordic Summit, and press freedom storm over journalist Helle Lyng
stories.summary: Indian PM Narendra Modi visited Oslo on May 18–19 for the first Indian PM visit in 43 years, meeting PM Støre at Akershus Castle and King Harald V at the Royal Palace, receiving the Grand Cross of the Royal Norwegian Order of Merit, and signing 12 agreements on green energy, space, health and digital cooperation elevating ties to a 'Green Strategic Partnership.' The visit was overshadowed by a viral incident in which Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng questioned Modi about press freedom at their joint press conference, prompting her Meta accounts to be suspended, an international backlash from Indian nationalists, and a wider debate on India's press freedom record.

stories.headline: NATO foreign ministers meet in Helsingborg as Barth Eide presses for orderly US drawdown and European defence buildup
stories.summary: NATO foreign ministers convened in Helsingborg, Sweden on May 21–22 for the alliance's first meeting on Swedish soil, with Norwegian FM Barth Eide urging that any US troop reduction happen 'in a structured manner' to allow Europe to build up. Secretary of State Rubio warned allies the US drawdown would continue while Trump announced an additional 5,000 troops for Poland, causing confusion. Barth Eide stated European defence industries are 'enormously behind' required capacity and called for nuclear deterrence to remain transatlantic.

stories.headline: FrP polls at 20-year high as Listhaug dominates Norwegian politics
stories.summary: Multiple polls published in the week of May 19–24 show Fremskrittspartiet (FrP) and leader Sylvi Listhaug at their highest ratings since 2008, with one Norstat poll for NRK placing FrP at 31.4%, nearly double Høyre. Commentators attribute the surge to voter discontent over energy prices, interest rates, and immigration, with Listhaug capitalizing on government criticism in Stortinget's question hour.

stories.headline: Equinor and Aker BP agree NCS portfolio swap to accelerate North Sea and Barents Sea development
stories.summary: Equinor and Aker BP signed a strategic collaboration agreement involving a series of asset exchanges on the Norwegian Continental Shelf, including Equinor divesting a 19% stake in Ringvei Vest discoveries to Aker BP and increasing its Wisting discovery stake from 35% to 42.5%, plus a 38.16% Frigg UK licence transfer and a $23m cash payment from Aker BP. The deal aims to accelerate development of undeveloped fields and increase long-term production value.

stories.headline: Equinor warns Europe faces critical gas shortage if Hormuz disruption lasts 1–3 more months
stories.summary: Senior Equinor executives warned publicly that European gas storage, already critically low entering the summer refill season, could reach crisis levels if disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz continue for another one to three months, potentially pushing Dutch TTF prices toward €90/MWh and forcing industrial demand destruction. Equinor simultaneously signed a new five-year gas supply deal with Dutch firm Eneco and announced plans to invest $6bn/year to 2035 to maintain NCS output as Norway doubles down on European gas supply.

stories.headline: Russia's massive hypersonic missile attack on Kyiv prompts Støre to condemn 'total absence of will for peace'
stories.summary: Following Russia's overnight attack on Kyiv using hypersonic Oreshnik missiles, described as unlike anything seen before in scale, PM Støre spoke Sunday morning with President Zelensky and Ukrainian PM Svyrydenko to express Norway's support and condemned the attack as a 'total absence of will toward peace.' Zelensky publicly thanked Støre among European leaders who contacted him after the strikes.

stories.headline: Norway deepens EU integration through Baltic Sea strategy membership and military mobility observer status request
stories.summary: Norway formally joined the EU's Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region (EUSBSR) on May 18, becoming the ninth member with FM Barth Eide citing security imperatives. Separately, Norway formally requested observer status in the EU Council to participate in decisions on military mobility under the EU's new EMERS crisis framework — described as the first such request outside Schengen — ahead of a key EØS Council meeting where Barth Eide will face EU officials on the energy directive backlog.

stories.headline: Listhaug attacks Støre over 'politically created' power shortage in Northern Norway as Melkøya electrification fails
stories.summary: FrP leader Sylvi Listhaug confronted PM Støre in Stortinget's question hour over a power shortage in Northern Norway, blaming Arbeiderpartiet for overriding common sense to electrify Melkøya with power the grid cannot supply. Støre faces criticism from FrP and the opposition that broken campaign promises on interest rate cuts and energy policy have created a governing crisis. Listhaug also challenged the government on the Morrow battery factory billions and on fuel tax cuts.

stories.headline: FrP's Jon Helgheim faces complaint and calls to resign from justice committee chair after sharing unblurred Bergen assault image
stories.summary: FrP's Jon Helgheim, chair of Stortinget's justice committee, shared unblurred images of suspects in a 17. mai gang assault in Bergen, triggering a formal complaint from one of the suspects, calls from MDG leader Hermstad for Helgheim to step down, and criticism from other parties. FrP leader Listhaug called for general caution about publishing identifying images while defending the substance of the debate on immigrant crime.

stories.headline: FrP adviser Kai-Morten Terning resigns amid racism scandal fallout
stories.summary: Kai-Morten Terning, a long-serving adviser to FrP leader Sylvi Listhaug in Stortinget's party group, resigned in the aftermath of the Hårek Hansen 'minor variants' racism scandal. Terning had been present with Hansen at the pub when the offensive remarks were made; he has since taken a new position with Oslo FrP's city council group. The departure signals ongoing internal reckoning within FrP over racist statements by affiliated figures.

stories.headline: Norway's 'total defence' buildup gains international attention as Storting defense long-term plan stalls
stories.summary: International media coverage (SCMP, Infobae) highlighted Norway's 2026 'total defence' programme, citing PM Støre's warning that 'war could come to Norway again' and the government's 115bn NOK additional defence investment. Separately, Storting negotiations over proposed adjustments to the defence long-term plan (LTP) broke down without agreement, with parties unable to align on the revisions; talks are continuing into the weekend.

stories.headline: Economist professor attacks Støre government for undermining Norges Bank independence through political rate promises
stories.summary: Economics professor Kjetil Storesletten (University of Minnesota, former Norges Bank board member) publicly criticised PM Støre and the political establishment for creating pressure on Norges Bank by promising voters interest rate cuts during the election campaign, arguing this worsened inflation by causing the central bank to act too late and too weakly. Norges Bank's Q2 2026 expectations survey simultaneously showed all respondents expecting higher price growth. Finance Minister Stoltenberg defended the government's record.
